data.name: Private Morning Sail
data.headline: 2.5 hours • Up to 12 guests • $20 off per child
data.description:
**The Sail:**
- This private morning sail is a great way to start the day. Mornings are best to go see San Diego’s wildlife such as the seals, because there is little wind and few waves, allowing us to easily cross over to Point Loma. The bay will most likely have a calm gentle surface, allowing us to go with our motor with minimal leaning.


**What to Expect:**
- We will open sails if weather permits, so expect a little bit of leaning. It can get chilly when on the water so remember to bring warm clothes. Life Jackets will need to be worn by all guests age 12 and under. There are life jackets for everyone on board.

- **Captain Gratuity:** 10-20% (optional but appreciated)
- **Parking Fees:** $16 per car for 2-3 hours in the marina parking lot (we currently do not have an onsite office)

In accordance with Coast Guard regulations, Bareboat Charters do not automatically include a captain. However, we have a roster list of skilled, USCG-licensed captains familiar with our program. If you choose this option, your total booking price **includes both the sailboat rental fee and the $125 captain fee**. We hold the captain's fee and pay it directly to the captain you chose on the day of your sail.

data.booking_notes:
#Arrival
- Please arrive **20 minutes before your tour** to allow enough time to find the meeting spot. The marina is big and can be tricky to navigate.

#Check-in & Paperwork
- You’ll sign a **bareboat contract and captain’s agreement** on the day of your sail.
- Meet your captain **15 minutes before departure** at our lockers next to **Gate 2** to complete this process.

#Waiver 
- We are at **Safe Harbor Sunroad Marina**, near **Gate 2 (middle gate)**.
- Parking rates: **2-3 hours: $16 | 3-5 hours: $20 | 5+ hours: $25**

#Captain's Fee & Tip
- The **$50 per hour captain’s fee** is already included in your booking and will be transferred to your chosen captain on the day of your sail.
- **Gratuity (10-20%)** is optional but appreciated.

#What to Bring
- **Clothing:** Hat, sunscreen, removable shoes, warm layers (sweater, windbreaker, warm pants).
- **Shoes:** We recommend going barefoot for stability. If needed, bring **non-slip socks or clean set of boat shoes** .
- **Food & Drinks:** You’re welcome to bring food and soft drinks. **Light alcohol is allowed in moderation**. No **hard liquor or red wine**.

#What to Expect
- **Duration:** 2.5 hours
- **Route:** From Safe Harbor Sunroad Marina, cruising down to Point Loma to see the Seals
- **Weather:** We may open sails if conditions allow, so expect a slight tilt. It can get chilly, so bring warm clothes.
- **Safety:** Life jackets required for kids 12 & under (provided on board).
data.faqs:
- **What Do We Need To Bring?**
-- We recommend bringing warm clothes, a hat, sunscreen and removable shoes.
For this experience, you are more than welcome to bring your own foods and soft drinks

- **Do We Need To Wear Lifejackets?**
-- Everyone 12 years and younger must wear life jackets while onboard the vessel.


- **When to be there**
-- Please arrive 20 minutes before, for the marina is big and it’s easy to get lost. Your captain will meet you at our lockers, right next to Gate 2 ( the middle most gate), 15 minutes before departure time.
Please arrive on time. Our trip will be cut short if we leave late.


- **What will we see?**
-- Excellent question! You will have 2 options for your sail
### Head to Coronado Bridge:
-  In this option, we will sail along the US Midway, see landmarks like the Kissing statue, the Rady Shell, seaport village, view Coronado island and we will go under the Coronado bridge.
### Go see the Seals
- This option is best in the morning when the winds are calmer. Here we will be sailing for around an hour there, circle the seals a few times, and head back. In some rare scenarios, you might view a dolphin or two.
